title: A Biologist’s Guide to Traction Force Microscopy Using Polydimethylsiloxane Substrate for Two-Dimensional Cell Cultures
protocol: Pipette equal weights of Cy-A and Cy-B using a P1000 cut tip into a weigh tray.
Stir PDMS mixture well with a P200 cut tip.
Add 0.08 g of PDMS mixture onto a glass bottom dish.
Drop the PDMS mixture at the center of the dish to generate an even layer of substrate coating.
Spin coat at 500 rpm for 30 seconds to generate a substrate thickness of >100 μm.
Cure PDMS substrate for 2 hours at 80°C.
Silanize PDMS surface.
Prepare 5% (v/v) APTES solution in 100% ethanol.
Add 2 mL of 5% APTES solution on cured PDMS dish for 10 min.
Remove 5% APTES solution and wash PDMS dish 3 times with 3 mL of 100% ethanol.
Dry PDMS dish at 80°C for 30 min with the lid ajar.
Prepare 5 mL of 0.05% (v/v) beads in distilled water.
Sonicate bead solution at around 50–60 Hz for 10 min.
Filter bead solution through a 0.45 μm filter.
Incubate PDMS dish with bead solution for 5 min at room temperature (∼22°C–25°C).
Remove bead solution and wash PDMS dish 3 times with 3 mL of distilled water.
Dry dish at 80°C for 15 min with the lid ajar.
Incubate dish with 3 mL of 100 mM Tris solution for 10 min at room temperature (∼22°C–25°C).
Remove Tris solution and wash PDMS dish 3 times with 3 mL of distilled water.
Dry dish at 80°C for 15 min with the lid ajar.
Prepare 50 μg/mL fibronectin solution in distilled water or 1× PBS.
Add 2 mL of fibronectin solution to PDMS dish.
Incubate PDMS dish at room temperature (∼22°C–25°C) for 1 h.
Remove fibronectin solution and wash PDMS dish 3 times with 3 mL of PBS.
Add 1 mL of 1% pluronic to PDMS dish for sterilization.
Incubate at room temperature (∼22°C–25°C) for 30 min.
Remove pluronic and wash PDMS dish 3 times with 3 mL of PBS.
Seed cells onto PDMS dish so that a confluent monolayer is established in 24 h.
Transfer dish to a widefield fluorescence microscope.
Acquire images of beads using a 10× or 20× dry objective.
Set up a single z-plane for imaging channels of beads and cells separately.
Capture images as tiff files.
Determine the duration and time interval for capturing the movie.
Capture an image every 15 minutes for 24 hours, if applicable.
Adjust the time interval based on cell movement speed.
Remove lid of the dish carefully at the end of a 24-h run.
Add 10% SDS to detach cells and obtain reference bead images.
Do not remove the dish from the microscope to prevent loss of imaging positions.
Capture reference bead images after approximately 1 hour when substrate deformation is fully reversed.
